title: Choose the visual world for the agent chat
question: The roll assigned the Identity Program direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Identity Program
options.lineage: Swiss/International Typographic Style corporate identity programs (Aicher, Müller-Brockmann)
options.thesis: The agent run as a numbered, colour-coded programme: every step has a module, and actions with side effects wait in an orange field until a human clears them.
options.viewport: Blue programme rail on the left with numbered step modules; transcript on a strict baseline grid; a pending action fills an orange docket under the transcript, written as one plain sentence with its arguments as a key/value table.
options.risk: Can read as a style exercise if the grid loosens or colour is used for decoration instead of state.

raised.raise: One colour owns every live state: orange means 'waiting for you', nothing else is ever orange.
While an approval is pending, the rest of the transcript dims so the decision is the only lit thing.
States are marks, not badges: hairline at rest, filled when cleared, struck through when rejected.
Tool output rides as its own layer, never in the agent's voice: a separate, labelled, inset band.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: no bubbles or shadows, only size, weight and the grid.

options.label: Clearance Strips
options.lineage: air traffic control flight progress strips
options.thesis: Every agent action is a strip on a board, and nothing moves until a human gives it clearance.
options.viewport: Conversation on the left; on the right a strip board where each tool call is a coloured strip, pending ones in the 'awaiting clearance' bay with Approve and Reject.
options.risk: The most literal reading of 'approval': it is where many runs would land, and it can become a costume of a control-tower tool.

options.label: Transit Line
options.thesis: The run is a line on a transit map: every step a station, an action with side effects a closed interchange you open by approving.
options.viewport: A vertical line down the left with a station per step; the pending action is an amber interchange that expands into the decision panel.
options.case: Holds product clarity (the run's progress reads at a glance), but office operators identify less with it than with an office identity programme.
options.risk: The map can upstage the conversation if stations grow larger than the text.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Flat colour tiles and giant cropped lowercase as the interface.
options.viewport: Panorama of tiles with giant lowercase headings.
options.case: Cropped display type fights reading long answers; operators do not need a panorama.
options.kept: One colour owns every live state.

options.label: Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles where the focused one expands and the rest dim.
options.case: A chat is a single thread, not a catalogue to browse.
options.kept: Dim everything except the pending decision.

options.label: Centre-Rail Setting
options.lineage: reference-setting with a centre key rail
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail of keys, states as printed marks.
options.viewport: Twin columns with a vermilion rail.
options.case: Bookish and dense; operators would read it as a document, not a tool.
options.kept: States are marks: hairline, filled, struck.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain below, a purple course above that never edits the terrain.
options.viewport: A map with the run drawn as a course.
options.case: Few operators know the notation; the metaphor needs explaining.
options.risk: Ornamental contours on a working screen.
options.kept: Untrusted output is a separate layer that never edits the agent's voice.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Giant letterforms, tiny mono labels, hierarchy by scale alone.
options.viewport: One giant glyph and a glyph grid.
options.case: No product fact maps to font axes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A centred chat column like the leading assistants, with an inline approval card, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centred conversation, composer pinned at the bottom, approval as a card inside the thread.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other agent demo by design.
